record.office: Chief Justice, Supreme Court of Alabama
record.t: Was elected chief justice of the Alabama Supreme Court in November 2024; took office in 2025.
record.q: Stewart Chief Justice 2025 - Present Supreme Court Associate Justice 2019 - 2025 Chief Justice Sarah Hicks Stewart was elected in November 2024 as Chief Justice of the Alabama Supreme Court.

record.t: Served six years as an associate justice of the Alabama Supreme Court (2019–2025).
record.q: Prior to her election, Chief Justice Stewart served as Associate Justice on the Alabama Supreme Court for six years.

record.t: Was appointed a circuit judge in Mobile by Gov. Bob Riley in 2006, the first female jury trial judge there.
record.q: When Chief Justice Stewart was appointed in 2006 by Governor Riley, she was the first female jury trial judge in Mobile.

record.t: Was elected the first female president of the Alabama Circuit Judges Association.
record.q: As a Circuit Judge, Chief Justice Stewart was active in the leadership of the Circuit Judges Association, serving as the state-wide Education Chair for eight years, and was elected by her fellow judges as the first female president of the Circuit Judges Association.

record.office: Chief Justice, Supreme Court of Alabama
record.t: Served on the Supreme Court's standing committee on the Alabama Rules of Evidence.
record.q: Chief Justice Stewart served as the co-chair on the Alabama State Bar's Professionalism in the Bench and Bar, on the Supreme Court's standing committee on the Alabama Rules of Evidence, and on many other Alabama State Bar and judicial committees.

record.t: Was in private practice for 14 years before joining the bench.
record.q: Prior to her appointment to the Circuit Bench in 2006, Chief Justice Stewart was in private practice for fourteen years.
